title: Bounded Dominican, Carmelite and Braga book states

traditions.label: Dominican use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the Order of Preachers; the selected original Latin printings, not a translation history.
traditions.coverage_note: Two page-collated states bracket intervening revisions; the 1604 printing witnesses a reform already described in 1602 and 1603.

traditions.label: Carmelite use
traditions.scope: Latin missals of the ancient observance of the Order of Carmel; not the Discalced Carmelites’ separate Roman-use books.
traditions.coverage_note: Two printings establish a bounded October calendar change. The precise intervening act is not yet identified.

traditions.label: Rite of Braga
traditions.scope: Bracarense Latin missals, kept distinct from Roman, Carmelite and Dominican uses.
traditions.coverage_note: 1538–1558 change is established through original scholarship. The 1924 approved state has direct prefatory evidence; its precise body revision remains open.

sources.title: Missale ad usum fratrum Praedicatorum Sancti Dominici (Venice, 1550)
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: title (PDF 5); fols 125r–125v (PDF 289–290), Suscepimus Deus formulary and beginning of the following Mass.
sources.limitations: Only the identified formulary and title were collated; whole-book continuity and precise intermediate ancestry are not inferred.

sources.title: Missale juxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum S. P. N. Dominici (Rome, 1604)
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: title (PDF 3), Clement VIII brief (PDF 5–6), Xavierre letter (PDF 7), pp. 238–239 (PDF 314–315).
sources.limitations: Title year is the printing date. The reprinted brief is dated 2 April 1602 and the letter 17 February 1603. Limited formulary comparison, not a complete transcription.

sources.title: William R. Bonniwell, A History of the Dominican Liturgy, second edition (1945)
sources.inspection: Printed pp. 320–321 read as page image (PDF 167); pp. 308–311 and 322–325 located in extracted text as contextual leads.
sources.limitations: Modern copyrighted scholarship retained only in scratch; no full-text import. Page-image-confirmed reform account is distinguished from OCR-only leads. Author’s judgments about reform are not adopted.

sources.title: Missale antique professionis Regularium beatissime Dei genitricis semperque virginis Marie de Monte Carmelo (Venice: Giunta, 1574)
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: title (PDF 7) and October calendar (PDF 20).
sources.limitations: Limited calendar sample, not complete sanctoral or Mass ordinary collation.

sources.title: Missale fratrum Carmelitarum Ordinis Beatae Dei Genitricis Mariae de monte Carmelo (Venice: Giunta, 1621)
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: title (PDF 3), Gregory XIII brief dated 26 September 1584 (PDF 5), October calendar (PDF 22), sanctoral p. 409 (PDF 462).
sources.limitations: The copy has handwritten changes, including the title and the Teresa sanctoral margin; only printed text supports the proposed stages. The 1584 instrument is reprinted, not a new act of 1621.

sources.title: Joaquim Félix de Carvalho, “A Liturgia em Braga”, Didaskalia 37 (2007), no. 2, pp. 139–184
sources.inspection: Page images inspected: printed pp. 162–165 (PDF 24–27), including 1538 colophon and 1558 pastoral excerpts, Ordo description and Palm Sunday comparison. Printed p. 176 consulted in extracted text only.
sources.limitations: Modern scholarship, not a primary-book collation by this researcher. Palm Sunday comparison reports Joaquim Bragança’s comparison in note 141. No full-text import; 1924 dependence noted on p. 176 remains an OCR-only lead.

stages.label: Venice witness before the Xavierre revision
stages.scope: Suscepimus Deus formulary within the temporale.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum fratrum Praedicatorum Sancti Dominici, Venice, 1550
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus appears under Dominica octava, with Deus cuius providentia as collect and Attendite a falsis prophetis as Gospel.

evidence.claim: Venice 1550 is printed on the title.
The named formulary and texts are visible on the identified folios.

stages.limitations: This does not reconstruct the full 1550 missal, identify its immediate exemplar, or establish how long each house used it.
stages.reception: The title identifies the Dominican use. A printed intended-use statement does not prove reception in every province.

stages.label: Xavierre revision witnessed in the Rome printing
stages.scope: A revised temporale formulary and the revision’s reprinted authorizing documents.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum S. P. N. Dominici, Rome, ex typographia Alfonsi Ciacconi, apud Carolum Vulliettum, 1604
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus now has Largire nobis as collect and the unjust-steward Gospel, with its heading moved to Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity.

evidence.claim: Printing dated 1604, under Hieronymus Xavierre.
The editor explicitly describes conformity of Epistles and Gospels to Roman use.
The revised combination is directly visible.

stages.limitations: The original intervention predates this printing; 1604 is not assigned as the first promulgation or first revised edition. Only the selected formulary is text-collated.
stages.reception: Clement VIII’s brief dated 2 April 1602 preserves the Order’s rite while authorizing conformity in specified matters. Its adoption windows depend on place and availability of copies; actual local uptake is not established.

stages.label: Carmelite October calendar before the later additions
stages.witness_label: Missale antique professionis Regularium beatissime Dei genitricis semperque virginis Marie de Monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1574
stages.summary: October 5 has no printed feast. October 6 includes Abraham, Isaac and Jacob with three lessons and the octave of Michael; October 8 includes Simeon the prophet.

evidence.claim: Imprint is Venice, Giunta, 1574; the book identifies the Carmelite observance and custom of Jerusalem.
These printed entries are directly visible.

stages.limitations: Calendar absence on one date is not proof that a saint or devotion is absent from every section of the volume.
stages.reception: This is the Carmelite Latin book identified by its own title. The title’s Jerusalem claim is recorded without constructing a genealogy from it.

stages.label: Carmelite calendar with Teresa of Jesus
stages.scope: Printed October calendar and Teresa’s printed common-Mass reference.
stages.witness_label: Missale fratrum Carmelitarum Ordinis Beatae Dei Genitricis Mariae de monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1621
stages.summary: October 5 prints Teresa as duplex minus with a commemoration of Placidus and companions. Teresa’s sanctoral entry directs the reader to the common Dilexisti iustitiam Mass.

evidence.claim: The 1621 printing is described as printed again, with chapter and Prior General authority.
Teresa’s feast and common-Mass reference are printed, distinct from marginal handwriting.
The instrument is dated 26 September 1584, not 1621.

stages.limitations: Neither the exact introduction date of Teresa’s feast nor the date of the chapter decree is established. Manuscript corrections in this copy are excluded.
stages.reception: The printed book belongs to the Carmelite ancient-observance sequence. A handwritten direction to a Discalced missal on p. 409 is not treated as the printed rite’s prescription.

stages.label: Braga state preceding Limpo’s revision
stages.scope: Identified edition, represented through critical discussion of its Ordo and Palm Sunday.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Lisbon: Germão Galharde, 1538; BNP RES-1633-A
stages.summary: The pre-Limpo witness used in the reported comparison.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1538 witness.
Colophon and comparison identify this state.

stages.limitations: Primary pages remain uninspected; catalogue colophon locator f. 184v differs from article f. 183v and needs reconciliation.
stages.reception: A book of the church of Braga; surviving print identification does not establish continuous archdiocesan use until 1558.

stages.label: Limpo’s revised Braga missal
stages.scope: Reported changes to the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta usum et ordinem Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, Lyon: Petrus Fradin, 1558; BnF B-1478
stages.summary: Limpo’s revision changes the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1558 witness.
Describes concrete revisions.

stages.limitations: Primary leaves were not reached; no word-for-word collation is claimed.
stages.reception: Revision for Braga. Limpo’s Carmelite membership does not establish derivation from a Carmelite missal; Carvalho rejects direct dependence on the Carmelite 1551 and Lyon 1556 books he compared.

stages.label: Braga typical edition approved in December 1924
stages.scope: The title edition and its binding approval/conformity rules; no complete body reconstruction.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Rome: Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis, 1924; title edition distinct from the digitized copy’s later supplements
stages.summary: Approved 8 December and declared typical 9 December 1924. Future Holy See changes to Masses already contained in it must be applied; newly imposed universal feasts must enter the Braga calendar.

evidence.claim: Identifies the revised 1924 Vatican printing.
The dateline is 8 December 1924; it directs the archdiocese’s priests to this missal.
The decree dated 9 December 1924 declares the edition typical and sets the future conformity and feast-insertion rules.

stages.limitations: These rules describe the 1924 state; their absence from 1558 has not been established. Later inserted feasts in this copy must not be assigned to 1924.
stages.reception: The bull requires this missal for priests of the Archdiocese of Braga. This establishes the contemporary prescription, not universal subsequent observance or present law.

changes.after: Heading: Dominica sexta in the sequence after the octave of Trinity.

evidence.locus: Brief PDF 5–6 and Xavierre letter PDF 7
evidence.claim: The instruments authorize and describe aligning Epistles and Gospels with Roman use while retaining the Order’s ancient rite.
Explains the recombination of the Sunday Masses and the retained chant elements.

transitions.limitations: This pairs the Suscepimus formulary, not an asserted identical modern Sunday. Introit, Debitores sumus epistle, Esto mihi gradual, Populum humilem offertory and Gustate communion persist in the inspected pair; secret and postcommunion also differ but are not encoded here. Intermediate Bettini and Castrucci revisions prevent an unsupported immediate 1550→1604 printing genealogy.

transitions.summary: Teresa appears on October 5; the October 6 and 8 entries seen in 1574 are absent from those dates in 1621.

changes.after: October 5: Teresa, duplex minus, with Placidus and companions commemorated.

evidence.claim: Printed October entries inspected.
Printed October entries inspected.

changes.before: October 6: Michael’s octave plus Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; October 8: Simeon the prophet.
changes.after: October 6 and October 8 are blank in the printed calendar.

evidence.claim: Printed October entries inspected.
Printed October entries inspected.
Printed October entries inspected.
Printed October entries inspected.
The printed Teresa entry supplies an associated common-Mass reference.

transitions.limitations: The result is a bounded calendar comparison. Blank dates do not prove complete suppression elsewhere. No causal connection to a particular chapter act is established; 1621 is the witness date, and the 1584 reprinted brief predates it.

transitions.summary: The 1558 revision changes the Ordo and reorganizes Palm Sunday.

changes.after: Fixed opening prayers with Ave Maria; offertory prayers added; Salve Regina at the end.
changes.locus_before: Earlier editions as compared in Carvalho p. 164
changes.locus_after: 1558 Ordo as described in Carvalho p. 164

evidence.claim: Reports these additions.

changes.before: Palm blessing: seven prayers and a preface.
changes.after: Six prayers and a preface; four older prayers retained in a new order.
changes.locus_before: 1538 and earlier editions: Carvalho p. 164 n. 141

evidence.claim: Reports Bragança’s comparison.
Describes Limpo’s revision and its comparison.

transitions.limitations: Scholarly description only; exact source-text ancestry remains unestablished. No direct dependence on a Carmelite missal is asserted.

transitions.summary: The 1924 typical edition succeeds the identified 1558 witness; a specific body-text revision between them is still unestablished.

evidence.claim: The earlier witness is identified.
The later edition and its typical status are directly attested.

transitions.limitations: This edge records chronology only. The 1924 future-adaptation rule is described in its stage; no unsupported before/after rule change is inferred.
